verifiedAgainst.note: Verified: project rules live in .cursor/rules as .mdc files and are version-controlled; plain .md files in that directory are ignored by the rules system. Front matter fields are description, globs, and alwaysApply. Four rule types: always apply, apply intelligently (by description), apply to specific files (by globs), apply manually (@-mention).

vendorFields.stubNote: Schema-valid and shipped, but ungated: no traceability gate and no fixture test. This is the one target with genuinely different assembly semantics — units are partitioned by path glob rather than budgeted into one file — which is why kind and scoping are first-class schema concepts even while the target is a stub (ADR-0013). Emitting it needs a glob per unit, and the corpus carries no path scoping to derive one from, so every rule would fall back to alwaysApply and prove nothing.
